title: Owned: choose CTS vs factoring to sketch (light)
stem_student:
You are given two equations in standard form and asked only to choose a suitable sketch strategy — not to finish a full sketch.

A) f(x) = x^2 − 5x + 6
B) g(x) = x^2 + 4x + 7

For each, say whether completing the square to find the vertex, or factoring to locate the x-intercepts, is the more suitable strategy, and give one reason. Do not use a formula.
stem_teacher: LLOVES-owned Analyze beat. A2.11 statement names completing the square and finding the vertex, or factoring if possible to locate the x-intercepts, as example strategies. This is not a Ministry sample (A2.11 examples array is empty). Do not teach or apply the quadratic formula (A1.6 parked).
answer: A) Factoring is suitable: x^2 − 5x + 6 = (x − 2)(x − 3), so the x-intercepts 2 and 3 are friendly. B) Completing the square is suitable: g(x) = (x + 2)^2 + 3 does not factor over the reals, so intercepts are not a sketch path; the vertex (−2, 3) is readable after CTS.
answer_verification: Author-computed. A factors as (x − 2)(x − 3). B: x^2 + 4x + 7 = (x + 2)^2 + 3; discriminant 16 − 28 < 0 so no real intercepts — mentioned only as a teacher check, not as a student discriminant lesson.
